description: “The Lymphatic Circulation: Understanding and Treating Pediatric Lymphatic Flow Disorders” Presented by: Gregory Adamson, MD Clinical Associate Professor Pediatric Cardiology Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford Planners expect learners to: 1. Describe the anatomy and physiology of the lymphatic circulation and explain how disrupted flow produces chylothorax, PLE, plastic bronchitis, and chylous ascites. 2. Identify infants and children with suspected lymphatic flow disorders and initiate appropriate workup, including referral for MR lymphangiogram. 3. Identify clinical scenarios where lymphatic disease is misattributed to common diagnoses and examine how diagnostic anchoring may delay recognition and treatment. description: How can digital PCR help researchers achieve greater confidence in gene expression analysis? Join us for a Lunch & Learn with QIAGEN exploring best practices for sample preparation and how QIAcuity® Digital PCR can support sensitive, precise, and reproducible gene expression measurements. The session will cover key steps in the sample preparation process, including sample stabilization, RNA preservation, and nucleic acid extraction, to help ensure high-quality results. Attendees will also learn how digital PCR enables sensitive, precise, and absolute quantification of gene expression targets without the need for standard curves. Multiplexed assays can further increase throughput, conserve valuable samples, and provide deeper biological insights by enabling simultaneous measurement of multiple gene targets in a single reaction. Michael Busche, Ph.D., Digital PCR Application Specialist at QIAGEN, will discuss how combining optimized sample preparation with QIAcuity® Digital PCR can help researchers address limitations of traditional qPCR and improve confidence in gene expression studies. Michael received his Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley in 2020 and completed postdoctoral training at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 2025. Drawing on his background in molecular genetics and genomics research, he supports researchers across North America in applying digital PCR to a wide range of biological and clinical applications. The session will conclude with an opportunity for questions and discussion about applications and workflows for gene expression analysis. Enjoy a complimentary lunch while connecting with colleagues and learning about advances in digital PCR and gene expression analysis. Seats are limited. Reserve your spot today: https://humangenetics.ucsf.edu/lunch-and-learn-tech-seminar-series-qiagen-0 We encourage you to share this invitation with colleagues and collaborators who may be interested. We look forward to seeing you!

description: 8-Week Mindfulness-Based Cancer Recovery Program Online Zoom program, with Valeria Galetto, PhD If you have received a cancer diagnosis, you know the emotional part can take a toll on you. Research shows that if you learn how to manage your stress and anxiety, you can improve your quality of life and become an active participant in your own recovery and survivorship. This program is based on Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), a therapeutic combination of mindfulness meditation, gentle yoga, and simple practices designed to let go of fears and concerns and focus on getting well. Please plan to attend all nine sessions (Including the Saturday Session). The mindfulness subject matter builds from one session to the next, so it is important that attendees can commit to at least 6 of the 8 class sessions to participate. Should these dates not be convenient, please reach out for alternative support at 415-885-3693. description: Psychedelic Medicines in Palliative Care Presented by Brian T. Anderson, MD, MSc Brian T. Anderson, MD, MSc, is a psychiatrist at Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, and an Assistant Clinical Professor in the UCSF Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences. He is a founding investigator at the UC Berkeley Center for the Science of Psychedelics and he is affiliated with UCSF Neuroscape. His research group takes a public health approach to conducting clinical trials and observational studies that seek to improve how we address suffering and despair among people living with serious medical illness and people who use drugs. For over 15 years Dr. Anderson has studied the medical and non-medical uses of controlled substances, with a focus on psychedelics used in therapeutic and religious settings. Learning Objectives: At the conclusion of the program, learners will be more able to: Differentiate the demoralization syndrome from clinical depression. Describe the current science and regulatory status of psychedelic medicines for patients with serious medical illness. Evaluate designs for studying if psilocybin could improve cancer survival. Continuing Education: This UCSF continuing education activity was planned and developed to: uphold academic standards to ensure balance, independence, objectivity, and scientific rigor; adhere to requirements to protect health information under the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA); and, include a mechanism to inform learners when unapproved or unlabeled uses of therapeutic products or agents are discussed or referenced. UCSF adheres to the ACCME’s Standards for Integrity and Independence in Accredited Continuing Education. Any individuals in a position to control the content of a CE activity, including content planners, reviewers, authors, presenters, moderators, panelists, or others are required to disclose all financial relationships with ineligible entities. All relevant financial relationships have been mitigated prior to the commencement of the activity. Accreditation: In support of improving patient care, the University of California, San Francisco Office of Continuing Medical Education (CME) is jointly accredited by the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME), the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), to provide continuing education for the healthcare team. This CME activity meets the requirements under California Assembly 1195, continuing education, and cultural and linguistic competency. UCSF designates this live activity for a maximum of 10 AMA PRA Category 1 credit(s)TM. Attendees should claim only the credit commensurate with the extent of their participation in the activity. The credit maximum above reflects all Osher Center for Integrative Health Grand Rounds sessions in Fiscal Year 2027. Up to 1 credit may be claimed against any individual session. description: Join UCSF researchers for a practical look at new generative AI models, tools, platforms and workflows designed to facilitate and expedite scientific research! Title: "Benchmarking Automated Scientific Enquiry: When AI co-scientists outpace peer review, what becomes the arbiter of truth?" Featured Speaker: Luca Foschini, PhD President & CEO, Sage Bionetworks Seminar 3-4pm, Networking Reception 4-5pm Share the Flyer! Bio: Luca Foschini, PhD, is President and CEO of Sage Bionetworks, a nonprofit that builds open infrastructure for biomedical data sharing, including the Synapse platform and community challenges such as DREAM. Before Sage he co-founded Evidation Health, where as Chief Data Scientist he spent over a decade leading research on wearable and real-world data for health. He holds a PhD in Computer Science from UC Santa Barbara, has published more than 70 peer-reviewed papers, and in a previous life represented Italy at the International Olympiad in Informatics. Abstract: In under two years, AI systems went from grade-school math to research-level problems, and the length of tasks an agent can complete reliably keeps doubling every few months. More than twenty AI co-scientists now promise to search the literature, generate hypotheses, analyze data and write up results. Do they reason like scientists? Recent evidence says not yet: agents often gather evidence and then ignore it, and better scaffolds barely help. The deeper problem is verification. AI moves fastest where answers can be checked instantly, as in code or proofs, while biology checks its claims at the pace of the wet lab and of peer review. I will walk through what works today, where these tools fail, and how benchmarks run as living community efforts, kept fresh and re-run on every new model, can keep us honest about what is still true., powered by Localist, the Community Event Platform

description: What helps people feel that they truly belong—and what happens when they do? Join the UCSF Climate and Belonging's Fostering Awareness Speaker Series on October 28th from 12:10–1:00 p.m. for The Science of Belonging, featuring UCSF’s Mica Estrada, PhD. Part of the Fostering Awareness: Dimensions of Belonging series, this session will explore the research behind belonging and the ways our environments, relationships, and everyday interactions can influence whether people feel valued, connected, and able to thrive. Dr. Estrada is Associate Dean of Opportunity & Engagement and Professor in the UCSF School of Nursing. Her research examines social influence, identity, values, kindness, well-being, mentorship, and approaches that strengthen inclusion and persistence in STEMM communities.
